headline: Hot inflation data and a Nvidia scandal curb the bounce
body: Tuesday's rally attempt stalled after October CPI came in hotter than expected, reviving doubts about how much further the Fed can ease. The S&P 500 slipped 0.38% to 7,520.93, the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.74% to 25,065.87, and the Dow eased 0.30%, while the 10-year Treasury yield pushed up toward 4.98%. Technology was the day's weakest sector. The pullback is modest in index terms, but it lands on top of a shakier backdrop: CNN's Fear & Greed gauge had dropped into the low-20s, extreme-fear territory, earlier this week after a sharp sell-off, and Monday's broad snapback has not fully restored conviction. Breadth remains narrow, with the market still leaning on a handful of large-cap names to carry the tape.

Nvidia is now a story of its own on top of the macro one: the board opened an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over an alleged foreign-espionage approach, sending shares down as much as 8% intraday before they pared the loss, adding to a stock that was already roughly 21% off its early-October high. With Nvidia's earnings and a congressional briefing both due next week, the name looks set to keep driving AI-sector sentiment somewhat independently of the broader rate debate. Retail-chatter trackers didn't surface a clear, current read today, so this take leans more on price action and headline flow than on social-media positioning.
